entry: Person who uses written words to communicate ideas, inspire feelings and emotions, or entertain. Writers produce [[Novel|novels]], short stories, plays, screenplays, [[Song|songs]], [[Essay|essays]], reports, educational material and news articles, and their works are published in a wide range of media. Some combine text with drawings, graphics or multimedia, and some work from an oral tradition. Many write about their own writing process and motivation, or comment on other writers' work as criticism. Payment is only one motivation, and many writers are not paid for their work. The term is also used as a synonym of author, although author more often refers to legal responsibility for a piece of writing and to the writer of a book.

City, capital of Lower Silesian Voivodeship in southwestern [[Poland]] (pop., 2025: 672,545). Historically the largest city and capital of [[Silesia]], Wrocław lies on the Oder (Odra) River, and its metropolitan area has about 1.25 million people. It emerged as an early medieval settlement and became part of the Piast-ruled Polish state in the late 10th century. In the 14th century it passed to the Bohemian Crown, later coming under Austrian and Prussian rule before joining the [[German Empire]] in 1871 under the German name Breslau. After [[World War II]] it became part of Poland, most German residents fled or were expelled, and Polish settlers arrived. The city has a student population of over 130,000. Landmarks include Cathedral Island and the Centennial Hall, a [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage Site]].

[[Alloy|Iron alloy]] with a very low carbon content, in contrast to [[Cast iron|cast iron]]. It is made by puddling, melting high-carbon cast iron in a [[Charcoal|charcoal]] or coke hearth so that the excess carbon oxidizes. The iron is never fully molten, so impurities remain, and its fibrous slag inclusions give it a wood-like grain. It is tough, malleable, ductile and easily forge welded. Before effective steelmaking, wrought iron was the most common malleable iron, used for [[Rivet|rivets]], [[Nail (fastener)|nails]], wire, [[Chain|chains]], rails, pipes and horseshoes. Its use peaked in the 1860s, then declined as cheaper [[Steel|steel]] became available. Commercial production has ceased, and products sold as wrought iron are usually mild steel.

Group of [[Chinese language|Chinese]] varieties spoken at and south of the [[Yangtze]] delta. Wu is spoken primarily in [[Shanghai]], [[Zhejiang]] province and parts of [[Jiangsu]] province, and it is at times simply called Shanghainese. The Suzhounese variety was the prestige dialect of Wu in the 19th century, but Shanghainese had replaced it by the turn of the 20th century. Northern Wu varieties form a mutually intelligible language family, while Southern Wu varieties are not mutually intelligible. Linguists value Wu for preserving all voiced initials of medieval Chinese and the checked tone as a glottal stop. Wu, especially the Suzhou variety, is traditionally perceived as soft, leading to the idiom "the tender speech of Wu." Most speakers refer only to their local variety rather than to the group as a whole.

American hip-hop group formed in Staten Island, [[New York City]], in 1992. Members include RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, Inspectah Deck, U-God and Masta Killa, plus Ol' Dirty Bastard until his death in 2004. Its debut album, *Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)* (1993), is widely considered one of the greatest hip-hop albums. *Wu-Tang Forever* (1997) debuted atop the *Billboard* 200. The only copy of *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* was bought for $2 million by [[Martin Shkreli]]. The group was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2026.

Chinese empress (r. 690–705), the only undisputed female sovereign in Chinese history. Wu was a concubine of Emperor Taizong, then empress consort of Emperor Gaozong from 655. After Gaozong suffered a stroke in 660, she effectively ruled until his death in 683, then governed for her sons. In 690 she proclaimed the [[Zhou dynasty]] in place of the [[Tang dynasty]] and crowned herself emperor. Over a 45-year de facto rule she used informants and strict legal measures, purged members of the Tang royal house, reformed the civil service to promote merit, and patronized [[Buddhism]], literature and the arts. Her rule formed part of the High Tang period, though her later governance became increasingly autocratic. She was removed in the Shenlong Coup, which restored the Tang, and died a few months later.

City, capital of [[Hubei]] province in central [[China]]. Formed by the merger of Wuchang, Hankou and Hanyang, Wuhan lies at the confluence of the [[Yangtze]] and Han rivers and is a major transportation hub. The 1911 Wuchang Uprising against the [[Qing dynasty]] ended 2,000 years of dynastic rule. In 1938 the city was the site of the Battle of Wuhan during the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]]. [[SARS-CoV-2]], which later caused the COVID-19 pandemic, was first discovered in Wuhan on December 31, 2019, and the city was the location of the first lockdown of the pandemic in January 2020. It is a manufacturing and scientific center, home to Wuhan University and Huazhong University of Science and Technology.

Novel by [[Emily Brontë]], first published in 1847 under the pen name Ellis Bell. It concerns two landowning families on the [[West Yorkshire]] moors, the Earnshaws and the Lintons, and their turbulent relationships with the Earnshaws' foster son, Heathcliff. Driven by love, possession, revenge and reconciliation, it is influenced by [[Romanticism]] and [[Gothic fiction]]. Contemporary reviews were polarized, and the novel was controversial for its depictions of cruelty and domestic abuse and for its challenges to Victorian morality and class. [[Charlotte Brontë]] edited a second edition after Emily's death, published in 1850. It is now considered one of the greatest novels written in English and has inspired many adaptations.

Genre of Chinese fiction and low fantasy about martial artists in ancient China. The name combines wǔ ('martial') and xiá ('chivalrous'). Heroes usually serve no lord and often come from the lower classes, and a [[Chivalry|code of chivalry]] requires them to right wrongs. Stories of xia date back more than 2,000 years, and [[Sima Qian]] recorded assassins of the [[Warring States period]]. The genre flourished in the [[Tang dynasty]] and has been adapted for opera, films, television and video games. [[Jin Yong]]'s epic novels are among its best-known modern works.

American lawman and gambler, known for the [[Gunfight at the O.K. Corral|gunfight at the O.K. Corral]] in Tombstone, Arizona, in 1881. Earp served as assistant marshal to his brother Virgil in Tombstone. Earlier he had served in Wichita and Dodge City, Kansas. In the 1881 gunfight, Earp and his allies killed three Cowboys, and in the following months Virgil was maimed and Morgan was murdered. Earp was never wounded in the gunfights. Later he refereed a controversial boxing match. A 1931 biography, Stuart N. Lake's *Wyatt Earp: Frontier Marshal*, created his reputation as a fearless lawman.

Landlocked U.S. state in the Mountain West (pop., 2024: 587,618). Wyoming is the least populous state despite being the tenth-largest by area. Its western half consists of [[Rocky Mountains|Rocky Mountain]] ranges, and its eastern half is high-elevation prairie. The federal government owns just under half the land, including two [[National park|national parks]], Grand Teton and [[Yellowstone National Park|Yellowstone]]. Wyoming became the 44th state on July 10, 1890. It granted women the right to vote in 1869 as a territory, and in 1890 it became the first state to allow women to vote. Its economy relies on [[Tourism|tourism]] and minerals.

64-bit extension of the [[X86|x86]] instruction set, also known as AMD64. Announced in 1999 and first available in the AMD Opteron family in 2003, it adds a 64-bit mode with larger memory addressing and increases the general-purpose registers from 8 to 16. A compatibility mode lets 16-bit and 32-bit applications run unmodified alongside 64-bit programs. The original specification, created by AMD and released in 2000, was implemented by [[Intel]] and VIA Technologies. It was quickly adopted for desktop, laptop and server computers, and it effectively replaced the discontinued Intel Itanium architecture, with which it is not compatible.

Family of instruction set architectures, first developed by [[Intel]]. Based on the 8086 microprocessor introduced in 1978, the family takes its name from successors such as the 80186, 80286, 80386 and 80486. The term does not mean IBM PC compatibility, since embedded systems used x86 chips before the IBM PC appeared in 1981. As of June 2022, most desktop and laptop computers sold were x86-based, while [[Smartphone|smartphones]] and tablets are dominated by ARM. x86 is also used in [[Video game console|video game consoles]], workstations, servers and most new supercomputer clusters on the TOP500 list.

[[Superhero]] team of mutants in [[Marvel Comics]]. Created by [[Stan Lee]] and [[Jack Kirby]], the team first appeared in *The X-Men* #1 in September 1963. Mutants are humans born with the X-gene, which generally manifests during puberty, and prejudice against them is a frequent theme. Telepath Charles Xavier leads the team. Stories often involve [[Magneto (Marvel Comics)|Magneto]], an old friend and foil to Xavier who is sometimes an adversary and sometimes an ally. The series was canceled in 1970 for low sales, but after its 1975 revival under writer Chris Claremont it became one of Marvel's most successful franchises.

Form of high-energy electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength shorter than ultraviolet and longer than gamma rays. X-rays have wavelengths from 10 nanometers to 10 picometers and photon energies from 100 eV to 100 keV. Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discovered them in 1895 and named them X-radiation for an unknown type of radiation. They penetrate many solid substances, so [[Radiography|X-ray radiography]] is widely used in medical diagnostics, such as checking for broken bones, and in materials science. X-rays are ionizing radiation, and exposure can cause DNA damage, cancer and, at higher intensities, burns and radiation sickness. Their generation and use are strictly controlled by public health authorities.

American [[Social networking service|social networking service]], formerly known as Twitter. Users share short posts with text, images and video, and they can vote on context added through Community Notes. It was launched in 2006 as twttr and renamed Twitter months later. Posts were limited to 140 characters until 2017, when the limit rose to 280. [[Elon Musk]] acquired Twitter in October 2022 for US$44 billion and rebranded it as X in July 2023. In March 2025 X Corp. was acquired by xAI, and in February 2026 xAI was acquired by [[SpaceX]]. Critics have linked the platform to increased disinformation and hate speech.

Video gaming brand owned by [[Microsoft]]. The brand was introduced in the United States in November 2001 with the original [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] console, and it now covers four main home console lines, the Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming service and online services such as Xbox Game Pass. Microsoft's second console was the [[Xbox 360]] (2005), followed by the [[Xbox One]] (2013) and the Xbox Series X and Series S (2020). In 2019 Microsoft Studios was renamed Xbox Game Studios, reflecting the brand's expansion beyond hardware.

Seventh-generation home video game console made by [[Microsoft]]. Unveiled on May 12, 2005, it succeeded the original [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] and competed mainly with the [[PlayStation 3]] and Nintendo's [[Wii]]. Its Xbox Live service offered online play, digital downloads and streaming of music, television and films. Launched worldwide mostly between November 2005 and December 2006, it was initially in short supply, and early models had a high failure rate known as the "Red Ring of Death." It is the highest-selling console made by an American company. Microsoft announced in 2016 that it would end production of new hardware.

Home video game console developed by [[Microsoft]]. Released in November 2013 as the successor to the [[Xbox 360]], it was marketed as an all-in-one entertainment system. It returned to an x86 architecture, using an [[AMD]] accelerated processing unit built around the [[X86-64|x86-64]] instruction set. Its features included Blu-ray playback, live television overlay, cloud computing and sharing of gameplay to [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]]. Microsoft reversed early policies on internet checks and used-game resale after consumer backlash. The Xbox One S (2016) and Xbox One X (2017) followed, and production of all Xbox One consoles ceased at the end of 2020.

Home video game console developed by [[Microsoft]], the first in the Xbox line. Released in North America on November 15, 2001, it was built around standard PC components, including an [[Intel]] Pentium III CPU and an [[Nvidia]] GeForce 3-based GPU, and it ran variations of Windows 2000 and DirectX. It had a built-in hard disk and Ethernet connectivity. Cumulative sales reached 24 million units, 16 million of them in North America, but Microsoft lost over $4 billion on the console because manufacturing costs exceeded its retail price. Microsoft discontinued the Xbox in 2006 and closed its online services in 2010.

Chemical element (symbol Xe) with atomic number 54. Xenon is a dense, colorless, odorless [[Noble gas|noble gas]] found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts. Long considered inert, it formed the first known noble gas compound, xenon hexafluoroplatinate, when Neil Bartlett mixed xenon with platinum hexafluoride on March 23, 1962. Discovered in 1898 by William Ramsay and Morris Travers in the residue of evaporated liquid air, it was named from a Greek word meaning "foreign" or "strange." Xenon is used in flash lamps and arc lamps and as a general [[Anesthesia|anesthetic]], and it propels ion thrusters in spacecraft. Radioactive xenon-135, produced by beta decay of iodine-135 from [[Nuclear fission|nuclear fission]], is the most significant and unwanted neutron absorber in [[Nuclear reactor|nuclear reactors]].

[[Athens|Athenian]] military leader, historian and philosopher. At the age of 30 he was elected one of the leaders of the Ten Thousand, Greek mercenaries who retreated after the failed attempt of Cyrus the Younger to seize the [[Achaemenid Empire]]. His *Anabasis* recounts that march to the [[Black Sea]]. He associated with [[Socrates]] in his youth, and he later wrote about [[Sparta]], much of whose society is known largely through his works. His *Hellenica* continues [[Thucydides]]' history of the [[Peloponnesian War]]. His *Cyropaedia*, a semi-fictional biography of [[Cyrus the Great]], explores ideal rulership. He was known as the "Attic Muse" for the sweetness of his diction.

King of Kings of the [[Achaemenid Empire]] (r. 486–465 BC). The son of [[Darius the Great]], he inherited a multi-ethnic empire and suppressed revolts in Egypt and Babylon before invading Greece in 480 BC. He crossed the Hellespont, won at Thermopylae and Artemisium, and captured and razed [[Athens]]. After losing at Salamis he withdrew most of his army to Asia, and Mardonius was defeated at Plataea the following year. Afterward Xerxes oversaw large building projects at [[Persepolis]], including the Gate of All Nations and the Apadana, and continued work on the palace at [[Susa]]. In 465 BC he was assassinated by Artabanus, commander of the royal bodyguard, and his third son took the throne as Artaxerxes I.

Chinese politician, general secretary of the [[Chinese Communist Party]] since 2012 and president of China since 2013. The son of revolutionary veteran Xi Zhongxun, he was sent to rural Shaanxi during the [[Cultural Revolution]] after his father was purged. He studied chemical engineering at [[Tsinghua University]], then served as governor of Fujian and of Zhejiang before becoming vice president in 2008. As leader he has overseen an anti-corruption campaign, restructured the [[People's Liberation Army]], and increased state control over the economy. Critics argue that the campaign also purges rivals. In 2018 the constitution was amended to remove presidential term limits. The [[Belt and Road Initiative]] expanded China's economic presence abroad, and the 2020 [[Hong Kong]] national security law, which critics say effectively suppressed the city's pro-democracy camp, was enacted under his leadership.

Sub-provincial city, capital of Shaanxi in northwestern [[China]] (pop., 2025: 13.24 million). Known as Chang'an for much of its history, Xi'an is one of China's Five Great Ancient Capitals, having held that status under the Western Zhou, Qin, Western Han, Sui, Northern Zhou and Tang dynasties. The name Xi'an was adopted in 1369 under the early Ming dynasty. Its Mausoleum of the [[Qin Shi Huang|First Qin Emperor]] contains the [[Terracotta Army]], and five component sites form part of the [[UNESCO]]-listed [[Silk Road|Silk Roads]]. Since the 1980s the city has developed into a cultural, industrial, educational and research hub. It is home to Xi'an Jiaotong University and Northwestern Polytechnical University.
